newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin orders Russia troops pullout from Chechnya.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin orders Russia troops pullout from Chechnya.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin on Saturday ordered the withdrawal of two brigades from Chechnya to facilitate a peace settlement in the breakaway Russian region and the holding of elections there, the Kremlin press service said.

A senior military official told Reuters the two units -- brigade No 101 of the Interior Ministry troops and brigade No 205 of the armed forces were the last remaining Moscow troops in Chechnya. The rebel government had insisted they be pulled out.

Most Russian troops have already left Chechnya, scene of 21 months of fierce fighting in which tens of thousands died. Moscow had wanted the two brigades to stay in Chechnya on a permanent basis but rebels insisted all Russian troops leave.
Yeltsin's decree did not put any deadline for withdrawal but ordered the government to do it in a "planned manner".

The document was named "On measures to secure further peaceful settlement in the Chechen Republic". It said it was aimed at "reaching accord in society, furthering a peace settlement and demilitarisation of the Chechen Republic".

Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and Aslan Maskhadov, the head of the Chechen rebel government which controls the breakaway region, are due to meet in Moscow on Saturday to sign a new accord.
